# RIID-4653: Session Actor Migration

[Back to distribution-host-integration](../distribution-host-integration.md)

This slice moves the provider-neutral C4 run-scope session actor.

## Moved Surfaces

- `internal/agentbridge/session`
- docs updates in provider-runtime and daemon migration SSOT files
- focused public CI for session backpressure, timeout/cancellation, process exit ordering, protocol-driver lifecycle, telemetry extraction, tool-start blocking, and adapter temp-file cleanup gates

The session actor connects Process -> Parser/ProtocolDriver -> reducer -> bounded Events/Result streams for a single provider run. It is provider-neutral and uses only the public `internal/process` port plus public `internal/agentbridge` domain.

This slice does not move runtimeactor, supervisor, bridge/controlplane, concrete provider adapters, task DB/project/mwsd local API packages, provider-native approval RPC/hook implementations, packaging artifacts, private infra, secrets, or local machine state.

## RIID-5900 local claim termination observation

A private claim tracker admits provider Process.Start immediately before the call, independently of whether a Submit caller receives its handle. Actual core child-exit observation closes each admitted invocation before Result. Generic start errors, missing exit observations, counter overflow, and a terminal seal with pending work remain permanently unknown. Host preparation and verification reserve work before their goroutine and finish the reservation before posting completion to the supervisor.

Only an authenticated fresh PollStart gives coverage. Same-epoch repeated polls retain the scope; missing scope, recovered PollActive, and restart remain unknown. Fallback and host correction retain the same scope. Sealing blocks new starts and freezes the aggregate once. started_invocations counts successful provider Process.Start calls only, not host commands or OS descendants.

The aggregate is carried in private context, never provider Result or metadata. The source-owned immutable claim binding is redacted in JSON and formatting. A real terminal event ACK precedes the device-authenticated local_invocations_quiescent receipt; needs-user-input Running events never send it. Known-proof failures retain the original lease for the existing terminal retry with the same terminal key and proof until terminal ACK is confirmed; after that, retry only the receipt. Unknown proofs finish normal terminal processing without a new outbox; the server stays unknown. No remote-provider, descendant, restart, idle, or user-access authorization is proved. A receipt route returning exactly 404 or 405 is an older-server unsupported observation: after the successful business terminal ACK, clean up normally and keep server proof unknown. Transport errors, invalid ACKs, and all other error statuses retain normal terminal retry.
